chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: Boozaire Kings get popular, house parties and Wilhelmina Breaux's dance
summary: The group played house parties and a ticketed party, and pianist Wilhelmina Breaux paid them $1.50 for a packed dance.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: So after that, man, I could kind of stay out late. And that went on. The Boozaire(?) Kings, we get popular. Now they want us for house parties. They say, "We could pay you all two dollars if you all come around, you'll all be at the party, all them little girls are gonna be there, and you'all can have all the cake and ice cream you'all want." So we played a couple of them.
Then a woman, her daughter was named Manuella, she was a good-time woman, nice, you know. But she knew all them
chicks that love a good time, all them cats that love a good time. She gave a party and printed tickets, boy, and her house and yard was loaded.
A ticket to play at the house, huh?
Yeah, that the Boozaire(?) Kings would be there. And we had made this name, our reputation. So we made what, made about five dollars a piece, man. That was a whole lot-ta money then, man.
And we got this name, then everybody wanted us. Then they wanted us in the Tremais(?)...

That's a section up there, above Esplanade. But we couldn't go across there, because you had to fight them little thugs up there. Then over the bridge was another section, and they couldn't go up there. You know, they had the gangs of kids...

Yeah. Same gangs as Chicago(?). So Wilhelmina Breaux(?) was a piano player, and she heard about everything in the whole Downtown, in this section where we had a (?) section, an eight-block section was the Boozaire(?) Kings. Because we'd be out there on Claiborne Avenue under the trees playing in the evening, and there

would be a crowd around us like this. Man, we celebrated. So she gave a dance at the Franz(?) Ami, which is the big Creole hall where all the muckamucks go, real staunch-down Creoles, Free Men of Color, all that shit. It said, "Wilhelmina Breaux Presents the Original Boozaire(?) Kings." And she gave this thing. And man, that fuckin' place was packed and jammed. And I didn't set no price for it. I should have known it; I'd been doing this long enough. When she got through, she gave us a dollar-and-a-half a piece. Boy, these place was loaded, and she was charging 50 cents...no, 25 and 35 cents to come in. And that place was packed and jammed. And it was a great big hall. My mother said, "What did Wilhelmina Breaux(?) pay you all?" I said, "A dollar and a half." She said, "That dirty bitch should've gave you'all more money."
